summary: A six-offence arrest recorded by troopers at Fairbanks on Oct. 10 was charged the following day on six counts, four of them felonies, led by first-degree burglary in a dwelling, a Class B felony. A second Fairbanks file charged a Class C felony domestic violence assault within the day of the arrest. A third file opened on Sunday carries no charge at all. Troopers reported a death at Fairbanks on Oct. 10 with no foul play suspected. The Alaska Court System's criminal dispositions report refreshed for the first time in six days and records the first-degree murder charge in 4FA-26-00112CR as dismissed on Oct. 8 after a finding that the defendant was incompetent, together with about twenty further Fairbanks closures. The weekly criminal charges report, run-stamped 9:00 p.m. Oct. 11, lists 39 Fairbanks cases, 4 at Nenana, 2 at Delta Junction and none at Healy for a seventeenth consecutive week.

entries.title: Six counts filed at Fairbanks over an Oct. 10 arrest, four of them felonies and three flagged domestic violence
body: A Fairbanks criminal case, 4FA-26-02067CR, was filed on Oct. 11 against Ryan Bud James on six counts, all offence-dated Oct. 10 at Fairbanks. Count 1 is burglary in the first degree, in a dwelling, AS 11.46.300(a)(1), a Class B felony, recorded as domestic violence related. Count 2 is criminal trespass in the first degree, in a dwelling, AS 11.46.320(a)(2), a Class A misdemeanour, recorded as domestic violence related. Count 3 is vehicle theft in the first degree, AS 11.46.360(a)(1), a Class C felony. Count 4 is criminal mischief in the third degree, damage of $750 or more, AS 11.46.482(a)(1), a Class C felony, recorded as domestic violence related. Counts 5 and 6 are assault in the third degree, cause fear of injury with a weapon, AS 11.41.220(a)(1)(A), both Class C felonies. The case judge is Temple.

The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26101276, posted at 11:57 p.m. on Oct. 10, records that troopers arrested a 46-year-old man of that name on Oct. 10 for domestic violence burglary, domestic violence criminal trespass, domestic violence criminal mischief, vehicle theft and two counts of assault in the third degree, and that he was remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center. The six charges recorded by the troopers and the six counts on the court file correspond offence for offence.

A separate Fairbanks case under the same name, 4FA-26-02035CR, was charged on Oct. 11 with one count of criminal trespass in the second degree, upon premises, AS 11.46.330(a)(1), a Class B misdemeanour, offence-dated Oct. 8. That case had carried no charging document since it was filed. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Class C felony assault with a weapon charged at Fairbanks within the day of the arrest
body: A Fairbanks criminal case, 4FA-26-02068CR, was filed on Oct. 11 against Robbie Dale Bevard on four counts, all offence-dated Oct. 11 at Fairbanks. Count 1 is assault in the third degree, cause injury with a weapon, AS 11.41.220(a)(1)(B), a Class C felony, recorded as domestic violence related. Count 2 is assault in the fourth degree, recklessly injure, AS 11.41.230(a)(1), a Class A misdemeanour, recorded as domestic violence related. Count 3 is interfering with a report of a domestic violence crime, AS 11.56.745, a Class A misdemeanour, recorded as domestic violence related. Count 4 is violating conditions of release for a misdemeanour, AS 11.56.757(a), a Class B misdemeanour. No judge was assigned on the file at the time of reading.

The Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin records the arrest at the 1900 block of Chena Landings Loop Road at 02:57 on Oct. 11 under case 26003119, giving the age as 52, on four charges that correspond to the four counts filed. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: A drink-driving arrest on Old Chena Pump Road, and the court file opened the same day carries no charge
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26101344, posted at 7:59 a.m. on Oct. 11, records that at about 12:03 a.m. a trooper stopped a pickup on Old Chena Pump Road in Fairbanks after it made a wide turn and failed to stop at a stop sign, that the driver showed signs of impairment, that a preliminary breath test measured 0.113 and a subsequent Datamaster test 0.135, and that the driver was arrested and charged with driving under the influence under AS 28.35.030.

A Fairbanks criminal case, 4FA-26-02066CR, was filed on Oct. 11 against Munoz Lee and carries one count recorded as Charging Document Pending or Not Filed, with no degree of offence, offence-dated Oct. 11 at Fairbanks. The case judge is Bahr. The court file records no docket entries. No charge class is stated because none appears on the file; the driving under the influence charge above is a charge recorded by the arresting agency, not a count on the court record. He is arrested, not convicted.

entries.title: Troopers report a death at Fairbanks on Oct. 10 with no foul play suspected
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26101215, posted at 9:48 a.m. on Oct. 11, records that on Oct. 10 at 13:23 troopers received a report of a death in Fairbanks and that investigation revealed that John Mayer Jr., a 51-year-old Fairbanks resident, had died. The release states that no foul play is suspected, that the State Medical Examiner's Office was notified, that the remains were released to his family and that next of kin were notified. The release states no manner of death and no criminal charge arises from it on any record read.

entries.title: First-degree murder charge recorded as dismissed on a finding of incompetency
body: The Alaska Court System's criminal dispositions report records case 4FA-26-00112CR, State of Alaska against Brian Jeffery Davenport, as disposed on Oct. 8, 2026. The single count, offence-dated Jan. 20, 2026, is murder in the first degree, intent to cause death, AS 11.41.100(a)(1)(A), and its disposition is recorded as Dismissed, Defendant Found Incompetent, dated Oct. 8, 2026.

Alaska CourtView records the same disposition date against the count, carries the docket entries recording it dated Oct. 9, and gives the case status as Closed. Charges that are dismissed are not convictions, and the court file states no finding about the alleged conduct. The Alaska Department of Law has published nothing about the case.

entries.title: The dispositions report refreshed after six days and adds about twenty Fairbanks closures
body: The Alaska Court System's criminal dispositions report now carries the footer stamp Data updated 10/12/2026 at 4:00 am and the header Case Closed Between: 9/1/2026 to 10/12/2026, after six consecutive days stamped 10/05/2026. The file runs to 237 pages, against 191. Read in full for the four Interior court prefixes, it carries 182 distinct Fairbanks case numbers, 11 at Nenana, 6 at Delta Junction and none at Healy.

Nineteen further Fairbanks closures and one at Nenana carry closing dates between Oct. 5 and Oct. 8. Among them: 4FA-25-01792CR, disposed Oct. 5, in which two counts of assault are recorded as Guilty Conviction After Guilty Plea and four further counts are recorded as dismissed by prosecution; 4FA-26-00387CR, disposed Oct. 6, in which two counts of assault in the fourth degree causing fear of injury, one count of driving under the influence and one count of violating a condition of release for a felony are all recorded as Guilty Conviction After Guilty Plea; 4FA-26-01025CR, disposed Oct. 6, in which unlawful contact in violation of a court order, driving under the influence and violating conditions of release are recorded as Guilty Conviction After Guilty Plea with seven further counts dismissed; 4FA-25-00957CR, disposed Oct. 5, criminal nonsupport, recorded as Guilty Conviction After Guilty Plea; and 4FA-26-01354CR, disposed Oct. 6, driving under the influence, recorded as Guilty Conviction After Guilty Plea. The remainder are dismissals.

The Fairbanks column rose by twenty-nine distinct case numbers while nineteen Fairbanks cases in the file carry closing dates inside the seven days the window gained. Either the file has added ten Fairbanks closures dated on or before Oct. 4 that were not in the previous version, or one of the two counts is wrong. This report states both figures and asserts neither.

entries.title: Weekly charges report: 39 Fairbanks cases, 4 at Nenana, 2 at Delta Junction, none at Healy for a seventeenth week
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly criminal charges report carries the stamp Report Run Date: 10/11/2026 9:00 pm and the window 10/5/2026 to 10/11/2026, across 56 pages. Read for the four Interior court prefixes, it lists 39 cases at Fairbanks, 4 at Nenana, 2 at Delta Junction and no Healy section at all, which is a seventeenth consecutive week. The word Healy does not appear anywhere in the report this week; last week it appeared three times as the offence location on a case filed at Nenana.

Three Fairbanks cases were filed on Sunday, Oct. 11: 4FA-26-02066CR, 4FA-26-02067CR and 4FA-26-02068CR, all carried above. No case was added to any earlier day in the window since the previous run. The Nenana cases are 4NE-26-00100CR filed Oct. 7, 4NE-26-00101CR and 4NE-26-00102CR filed Oct. 8 and 4NE-26-00103CR filed Oct. 10. The Delta Junction cases are 4DJ-26-00061CR filed Oct. 5 and 4DJ-26-00062CR filed Oct. 9.

The offence-location column records 79 charge lines at Fairbanks, 4 at North Pole, 8 at Delta Junction and 4 at Nenana, and none at Fort Wainwright, Eielson, Salcha, Minto, Anderson, Ester, Two Rivers, Moose Creek or Healy. Eleven cases in the Fairbanks area carry no charging document at the time of reading, four of them with no docket entries at all. The weekly window closes at 9 p.m. and is therefore short of its own last filing day.
